evidence: Nestled within the historic matrix of the 36 Old Streets in the heart of Hanoi, the capital city of Vietnam, Hang Ma Street stretches like a vibrant silk ribbon through the bustling Old Quarter. This narrow thoroughfare, rooted in the ancient land of Thăng Long, which boasts a thousand years of rich cultural heritage, derives its name from the traditional craft of making votive paper offerings and paper lanterns.

Historically, this street was home to families specializing in these crafts, serving sacred places and religious rituals, thus earning its Vietnamese name, Phố Hàng Mã, meaning "Street of Paper Offerings."
